SHOULD resolve prerequisites, parallelize independent calls. Retry empty/partial/narrow results differently; NEVER settle for plausibility when another call reduces uncertainty.

# 1. Scope

- Plan multi-file work before opening files.

# 2. Research Before Editing
- Read relevant sections; MUST reuse existing patterns, not establish a second convention.
  - Exported symbol changes: MUST run `lsp references` first.
- Tool failure or intervening file change: re-read before acting.

# 3. Decompose
- Update todos; skip trivial requests.
- NEVER make a todo-only turn; batch `init` with first work, `done` with next action/verification.

# 4. Implement
- Fix source, not symptoms or special-case inputs, unless asked.
- Cutover: migrate every caller; remove obsolete code/comments/aliases/re-exports/deprecated paths. Prefer existing files; review as user.
- Ask before destructive commands or deleting unrelated code you didn't write; code made obsolete by cutover is in scope.

Non-trivial work: NEVER yield without exercising the changed path. Tests alone are not proof.
- Investigation: run it; output proves it; no tests.
- UI: verify actual surface.

- Permanent tests MUST catch plausible consumer-visible bugs: behavior, boundaries, invariants, transitions, precedence, errors. Follow conventions; deterministic, isolated, full-suite-safe.
- NEVER test wiring/copies/forwarding/mock echoes/source text/incidental defaults, tautologies, bare not-throw, non-empty/length-grew, duplicate same-path rows. Use throwaway scripts.
- Existing wording/implementation/incidental-behavior tests: MUST delete, NEVER re-pin regardless of author.

After smoke proof: permanent fix/feature MUST update docs/changelog, remove scaffolds/throwaway scripts; tests per Verify. Investigation: no tests/docs. NEVER pre-plan cleanup todos.

patchManifest.description: OMP Desktop patch set for the pinned upstream OMP runtime: RPC host-tool scheduling and batch policy, settle-time run termination (result flag and per-tool settlement declaration), the all-toolCall batch count, an optional live system-prompt action for a host-confirmed mid-turn mode transition, a deterministic native-addon archive, and an explicit bytecode switch on the build entry. Risk reduction and release-build reproducibility only: it does NOT make the sole-batch contract strict — see status.

fork.note: Self-maintained fork whose HEAD is exactly base.sha + this patch level. `scripts/omp-sidecar.mjs` refuses any other commit; can1357/oh-my-pi stays a read-only upstream.

contract.invalidDeclaration: set_host_tools request is rejected; the value never degrades to the default
contract.invalidDeclarationDetail: RpcHostToolDefinition.concurrency/batchPolicy/terminateOnSettle values outside their union throw in normalizeHostToolPolicy, which the set_host_tools command and the host-tool adapter both call
contract.bytecodeBuildEntry: packages/coding-agent/scripts/build-binary.ts accepts exactly `--bytecode`/`--no-bytecode` (default on, one declaration, anything else exits 2); `compileCodingAgent` takes it as the typed option `CodingAgentCompileOptions.bytecode`, never from the environment
contract.liveSystemPromptAction: ExtensionAPI.setTurnSystemPrompt(prompt: string[]) — optional; a host that does not provide it rejects the call, and the desktop gate treats absence as a failed transition

history.retiredReason: T20-D-Enter added the optional live system-prompt extension action, which changed the patched tree; the .4 artifact bytes and fork coordinates are kept here as history.
T20-B2 added the settle-time termination declaration (AgentTool.terminateOnSettle), which changed the patched tree; the .3 artifact bytes and fork coordinates are kept here as history.

T20-R4-3 added the deterministic native-addon archive and the explicit bytecode build switch, which changed the patched tree; the .2 artifact and its file name are kept in git history, not in this tree.
T20-R4A migrated the patch set to the new pinned base 62bc57be (omp/18.3.0); the 18.2.7 artifact is kept in git history, not in this tree.

notes: This is an OMP Desktop-maintained patch level, not upstream OMP support: the runtime remains pinned at 62bc57be (omp/18.3.0) plus this patch set.

Rebuild the patch after any source edit with: git -C <checkout> -c core.abbrev=7 diff <base.sha> <fork.commit> > app/patches/oh-my-pi/0001-omp-desktop-runtime.patch, then refresh patch.sha256 and patch.bytes. The explicit core.abbrev=7 pins the index lines to 7 hex digits: a machine-level core.abbrev would otherwise change the patch bytes while preserving semantics, so the artifact could not be reproduced byte-for-byte elsewhere.

runner.initialize copies each ExtensionActions member onto the shared runtime explicitly; .5 therefore also copies the optional setTurnSystemPrompt action (with a refusing fallback), so a host that provides it is reachable through the extension API instead of the runtime's throwing stub.

The .5 patch artifact was regenerated on 2026-10-03 from fork commit 22f565c9403b5d5ce1870462529292d7a32fd550; it adds the optional ExtensionAPI.setTurnSystemPrompt action (AgentSession.setTurnSystemPrompt) so a trusted host with a host-confirmed mid-turn contract change (M5/T20-D's Agent -> Plan/Goal entry) can move the live run's system prompt before the next provider request. The action is optional and absent from every other ExtensionActions provider; ordinary runs are unchanged.

The .4 patch artifact was regenerated on 2026-10-03 from fork commit 512370a1b177cf45e4d12781104506ea372fb8a9; it adds the settle-time termination declaration (AgentTool.terminateOnSettle, RpcHostToolDefinition.terminateOnSettle) enforced at the loop's single settlement boundary, so a schema-validation rejection, a pre-execution hook rejection, an execution throw, a host error and a success all terminate identically for a declared tool.
The zero-side-effect property of a rejected mixed batch is unchanged by .4: a batch carrying a sole tool plus any sibling is still rejected whole with terminate false so the model can correct.

reproducible-sidecar-build: embed-native.ts writes the embedded addon tar.gz with fixed entry timestamps and a recomputed header checksum, because Bun.Archive stamps each entry with the current time. Without it, two builds of one fork commit produced different binaries — measured at T20-R4-3 on Bun 1.4.2 (first difference at byte 81260680).

explicit-bytecode-build-mode: bytecode stays on by default (upstream release behavior and the fast boot path). The desktop sidecar build passes `--bytecode` explicitly and records it as `build.bytecode` in the provenance manifest; measured reproducibility holds for bytecode on and off once the archive is deterministic.

status.blocker: F3: a `kCursorExecResolved` sibling was executed by the provider/editor bridge before the assistant message existed, so its side effect cannot be prevented or retracted by any loop-level patch; PI counts every toolCall block, so the batch is still rejected, but "zero side effects in a rejected batch" is unreachable at this layer.
mitigationsApplied: batch admission counts every toolCall block of the assistant message (Cursor-resolved included), matching PI runtime.ts:2222
speculation is disabled for a provider call whose active tool set advertises a sole-declared tool, so no speculative physical work starts before the batch decision
a declared settle-terminating host tool terminates the run on every settled result path, including a schema-validation rejection that never reaches execute
